fields.text: The Supporting Evidence Register is a list of all evidence contributing to the overall assessment outcome and any training information supplied to the candidate. This may include:
Certificates / Statement of Attainments (SoA)
Safe Work Procedures (SWP) and similar documents
Other relevant documents.

The Training and Assessment Record has been developed to provide a record of training and assessment against a unit of competency. The Competency Assessment Record (page 3) records all outcomes and decisions made against the relevant units and must be completed at the end of the assessment.

Training outcomes are recorded in the first four columns of each table and are grouped into the area of learning. Both the candidate and the trainer must initial and date the relevant columns to confirm that training has been satisfactorily completed. Each column is explained below.
Column 1 (Learning Criteria) contains the learning criteria to be covered.
Column 2 (Learning Content) lists sections in the reference material that address the area of learning.
Column 3 (Candidate Initials & Date) requires the candidate to sign and date as confirmation of their participation in the training and understanding of the content.
Column 4 (Trainer Initials & Date) requires the trainer to sign and date as confirmation that the candidate has covered the learning content.

Column 5 (Task) outlines the task to be completed by the candidate. All tasks are identified by a letter of the alphabet. These assessment tasks are mapped to the performance criteria of the national unit of competency. Oral questions are included to support tasks. Assessors are to record the candidate’s responses in the Comments box on the relevant page.

Column 6 (Observations) identifies the assessor’s observations. The candidate may perform other activities that demonstrate competence. Where applicable these should be recorded in the Comments box at the bottom of each page. Where a specific activity is not required or not observed include explanatory notes in the Comments box to ensure that the assessment meets the requirements of the unit of competency.

Column 7 (Assessor Initials & Date) records the outcome of the observation task. The assessor is to initial and date the column when the candidate has satisfactorily demonstrated capacity to complete the task to the specified requirements. Assessors should also consider the candidate’s capacity to apply the full range of knowledge and skills associated with the task.

sections.title: Trainer and Assessor Observations and Comments

fields.text: Comments should be recorded where the assessor has asked questions and gathered responses, or the assessment tool has been contextualised to meet candidate or workplace requirements. Fields have been provided at the bottom of each page to allow for this information to be recorded.

Qualifications certify the knowledge and skills that a person has achieved through study, training, work and life experience. When undertaking an assessment for any unit of competence, consider the guidelines for each level. The unit you are about to assess is a Level 3. Specific requirements for this level are detailed below.
Summary: Graduates at this level will have theoretical and practical knowledge and skills for work and/or further learning.
Knowledge: Graduates at this level will have basic factual, technical, procedural and some theoretical knowledge of a specific area of work and learning.

Skills: Graduates at this level will have basic, cognitive, technical and communication skills to select and apply a specialised range of methods, tools materials andinformation to: complete routine activities provide and transmit solutions to a predictable and sometimes unpredictable problems.

Application of knowledge and skills: Graduates at this level will apply knowledge and skills to demonstrate autonomy and judgement and to take limited responsibility in known and stable contexts and within established parameters.
Any feedback or comments you can provide on this training and/or assessment record is appreciated. Please detail your feedback in the space provided and send to the address below.
Thank you.
